answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie earning power to a slow-burning reputation ember: every agent starts dim and only brightens through verified, useful work attested by independent peers. A raven-fast flood of fresh identities gains nothing, because new accounts cannot spend or vote until their history proves real value. A prism of independent signals — work quality, peer attestations, and stake at risk — splits genuine contributors from copycat swarms, so creating a thousand fakes costs more than it can ever earn.
